   119→  def wetty_container_name(sandbox)

   131→  def container_running?(name)
   132→    container = Docker::Container.get(name)
   133→    container.json.dig("State", "Running") == true

   135→    false

   138→  def pull_image
   139→    Docker::Image.get(WETTY_IMAGE)
   140→  rescue Docker::Error::NotFoundError
   141→    Docker::Image.create("fromImage" => WETTY_IMAGE)
   142→  rescue Docker::Error::DockerError

   144→  end

   146→  def ensure_network
   147→    Docker::Network.get(NETWORK_NAME)
   148→  rescue Docker::Error::NotFoundError

   150→  end

   152→  def connect_sandbox_to_network(sandbox)
   153→    return unless sandbox.container_id.present?
   154→
   155→    network = Docker::Network.get(NETWORK_NAME)
   156→    container = Docker::Container.get(sandbox.container_id)
   157→
   158→    networks = container.json.dig("NetworkSettings", "Networks") || {}
   159→    return if networks.key?(NETWORK_NAME)
   160→
   161→    network.connect(sandbox.container_id)
   162→  end
   163→
   164→  def generate_keypair(sandbox)
   165→    key_dir = key_dir_path(sandbox)
   166→    FileUtils.mkdir_p(key_dir, mode: 0o700)
   167→
   168→    key_path = File.join(key_dir, "key")
   169→    # Remove old keys if they exist
   170→    FileUtils.rm_f(key_path)
   171→    FileUtils.rm_f("#{key_path}.pub")
   172→
   173→    system("ssh-keygen", "-t", "ed25519", "-f", key_path, "-N", "", "-q", "-C", "wetty-#{sandbox.full_name}",
   174→      exception: true)
   175→
   176→    # Ensure private key is only readable by owner
   177→    File.chmod(0o600, key_path)
   178→
   179→    key_dir
   180→  end
   181→
   182→  def inject_pubkey(sandbox, key_dir)
   183→    pubkey = File.read(File.join(key_dir, "key.pub")).strip
   184→    username = sandbox.user.name
   185→
   186→    container = Docker::Container.get(sandbox.container_id)
   187→
   188→    # Write pubkey via base64 to avoid any shell-injection risk.
   189→    # The stdin: approach hangs because docker-api never sends EOF to cat.
   190→    encoded = Base64.strict_encode64("#{pubkey}\n")
   191→    container.exec([ "mkdir", "-p", "/home/#{username}/.ssh" ])
   192→    container.exec([ "sh", "-c", "echo #{encoded} | base64 -d >> /home/#{username}/.ssh/authorized_keys" ])
   193→    container.exec([ "chown", "-R", "#{username}:#{username}", "/home/#{username}/.ssh" ])
   194→    container.exec([ "chmod", "600", "/home/#{username}/.ssh/authorized_keys" ])
   195→  end
   196→
   197→  def create_wetty_container(sandbox:, user:, key_dir:)
   198→    container_name = wetty_container_name(sandbox)
   199→
   200→    # Remove any existing container with this name
   201→    begin
   202→      old = Docker::Container.get(container_name)
   203→      old.stop(t: 3) rescue nil
   204→      old.delete(force: true)
   205→    rescue Docker::Error::NotFoundError
   206→      # No existing container
   207→    end
   208→
   209→    ssh_command = [
   210→      "ssh", "-p", "22",
   211→      "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=no",
   212→      "-o", "UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null",
   213→      "-o", "LogLevel=ERROR",
   214→      "-i", "/etc/wetty/key",
   215→      "#{user.name}@#{sandbox.full_name}",
   216→      "-t", "tmux new-session -A -s main"
   217→    ].join(" ")
   218→
   219→    container = Docker::Container.create(
   220→      "name" => container_name,
   221→      "Image" => WETTY_IMAGE,
   222→      "Env" => [
   223→        "COMMAND=#{ssh_command}",
   224→        "BASE=/terminal/#{sandbox.id}/wetty"
   225→      ],
   226→      "HostConfig" => {
   227→        "NetworkMode" => NETWORK_NAME,
   228→        "RestartPolicy" => { "Name" => "no" },
   229→        "Memory" => 128 * 1024 * 1024, # 128MB
   230→        "NanoCpus" => 500_000_000 # 0.5 CPU
   231→      },
   232→      "Labels" => {
   233→        "sandcastle.sandbox_id" => sandbox.id.to_s,
   234→        "sandcastle.role" => "wetty"
   235→      }
   236→    )
   237→
   238→    container.start
   239→    copy_key_to_container(container, key_dir)
   240→    container
   241→  end
   242→
   243→  # Copy the SSH private key into the WeTTY container via exec + base64.
   244→  # This avoids bind-mount path issues when Rails runs inside a container
   245→  # with a Docker volume for /data (the host path doesn't match).
   246→  def copy_key_to_container(container, key_dir)
   247→    key_content = File.read(File.join(key_dir, "key"))
   248→    encoded = Base64.strict_encode64(key_content)
   249→
   250→    container.exec([ "mkdir", "-p", "/etc/wetty" ])
   251→    container.exec([ "sh", "-c", "echo #{encoded} | base64 -d > /etc/wetty/key" ])
   252→    container.exec([ "chmod", "600", "/etc/wetty/key" ])
   253→  end
   254→
   255→  def write_traefik_config(sandbox)
   256→    FileUtils.mkdir_p(DYNAMIC_DIR)
   257→
   258→    host = ENV.fetch("SANDCASTLE_HOST", "localhost")
   259→    id = sandbox.id
   260→    container_name = wetty_container_name(sandbox)
   261→
   262→    rule = if ENV["SANDCASTLE_TLS_MODE"] == "selfsigned"
   263→      "HostRegexp(`.+`) && PathPrefix(`/terminal/#{id}/wetty`)"
   264→    else
   265→      "Host(`#{host}`) && PathPrefix(`/terminal/#{id}/wetty`)"
   266→    end
   267→
   268→    config = {
   269→      "http" => {
   270→        "routers" => {
   271→          "terminal-#{id}" => {
   272→            "rule" => rule,
   273→            "service" => "terminal-#{id}",
   274→            "entryPoints" => [ "websecure" ],
   275→            "tls" => tls_config,
   276→            "middlewares" => [ "terminal-auth-#{id}" ],
   277→            "priority" => 100
   278→          }
   279→        },
   280→        "middlewares" => {
   281→          "terminal-auth-#{id}" => {
   282→            "forwardAuth" => {
   283→              "address" => "http://sandcastle-web:80/terminal/auth",
   284→              "trustForwardHeader" => true
   285→            }
   286→          }
   287→        },
   288→        "services" => {
   289→          "terminal-#{id}" => {
   290→            "loadBalancer" => {
   291→              "servers" => [ { "url" => "http://#{container_name}:3000" } ]
   292→            }
   293→          }
   294→        }
   295→      }
   296→    }
   297→
   298→    File.write(File.join(DYNAMIC_DIR, "terminal-#{id}.yml"), config.to_yaml)
   299→  end
   300→
   301→  def tls_config
   302→    if ENV["SANDCASTLE_TLS_MODE"] == "selfsigned"
   303→      {}
   304→    else
   305→      { "certResolver" => "letsencrypt" }
   306→    end
   307→  end
   308→
   309→  def delete_traefik_config(sandbox)
   310→    path = File.join(DYNAMIC_DIR, "terminal-#{sandbox.id}.yml")
   311→    File.delete(path) if File.exist?(path)
   312→  end
   313→
   314→  def remove_pubkey(sandbox)
   315→    return unless sandbox.container_id.present?
   316→
   317→    begin
   318→      container = Docker::Container.get(sandbox.container_id)
   319→      username = sandbox.user.name
   320→      # Match end-of-line to avoid substring collisions
   321→      # (e.g. "wetty-user-foo" must not also remove "wetty-user-foobar").
   322→      # Sandbox names are [a-z0-9_-] only, so safe for regex.
   323→      marker = "wetty-#{sandbox.full_name}$"
   324→      container.exec([
   325→        "sh", "-c",
   326→        "grep -v '#{marker}' /home/#{username}/.ssh/authorized_keys > /tmp/ak_clean && " \
   327→        "mv /tmp/ak_clean /home/#{username}/.ssh/authorized_keys || true"
   328→      ])
   329→    rescue Docker::Error::NotFoundError, Docker::Error::DockerError
   330→      # Sandbox container gone or exec failed — best-effort
   331→    end
   332→  end
   333→end
   334→

```
class TerminalController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: :auth
  skip_before_action :require_password_change, only: :auth

  def open
    sandbox = if Current.user.admin?
      Sandbox.active.find(params[:id])
    else
      Current.user.sandboxes.active.find(params[:id])
    end

    path = TerminalManager.new.open(sandbox: sandbox)
    redirect_to terminal_redirect_url(path), allow_other_host: true, status: :see_other
  rescue TerminalManager::Error => e
    redirect_to root_path, alert: e.message
  end

  def close
    sandbox = if Current.user.admin?
      Sandbox.active.find(params[:id])
    else
      Current.user.sandboxes.active.find(params[:id])
    end

    TerminalManager.new.close(sandbox: sandbox)
    redirect_to root_path, notice: "Terminal closed"
  rescue TerminalManager::Error => e
    redirect_to root_path, alert: e.message
  end

  private

  # Build the full terminal URL. In production, Traefik is the entry point
  # so a relative path works. In local dev (selfsigned TLS), Rails may be
  # accessed directly on a different port, so we need an absolute URL.
  def terminal_redirect_url(path)
    base = ENV["SANDCASTLE_TERMINAL_URL"]
    base ? "#{base}#{path}" : path
  end

  public

  # Called by Traefik forwardAuth. Returns 200 to allow, or redirects to
  # login (which Traefik passes through to the browser).
  def auth
    forwarded_uri = request.headers["X-Forwarded-Uri"] || ""
    match = forwarded_uri.match(%r{/terminal/(\d+)/wetty})
    head(:unauthorized) and return unless match

    session_record = find_session_by_cookie
    unless session_record
      # Build the original terminal URL from Traefik's forwarded headers
      # so the user returns here after logging in.
      proto = request.headers["X-Forwarded-Proto"] || "https"
      host  = request.headers["X-Forwarded-Host"] || request.host_with_port
      original_url = "#{proto}://#{host}#{forwarded_uri}"
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = original_url
      redirect_to new_session_url, allow_other_host: true
      return
    end

    user = session_record.user
    sandbox = Sandbox.active.find_by(id: match[1].to_i)
    head(:unauthorized) and return unless sandbox && (sandbox.user_id == user.id || user.admin?)

    head :ok
  end
end
```

> AGENT

Found it. The `ContainerSyncJob` at line 30 only checks `State.Running` — it doesn't detect the "restarting" state:

```ruby
actual_status = container.json.dig("State", "Running") ? "running" : "stopped"
```

When a container is restarting, `Running` can flicker between true/false, so the sync job incorrectly considers it "running".

Here's a summary of all the issues I've found:

## Findings

### 1. Container in restart loop (immediate issue)
The sandbox container `8b184c75be23` is stuck in a Docker restart loop. This prevents `TerminalManager#open` from connecting it to the `sandcastle-web` network, so the terminal can't open.

### 2. Flash messages not rendered on dashboard
The layout (`application.html.erb`) doesn't render flash messages. Only specific views (admin settings, login, etc.) render them. The terminal error is silently swallowed. **Fixed locally.**

### 3. ContainerSyncJob doesn't detect "restarting" state
`sync_sandbox` uses `State.Running` which doesn't distinguish between truly running and restarting containers. A container in a restart loop may still show `Running: true` intermittently.

To diagnose *why* the container is crash-looping, I need SSH access to run `docker logs 8b184c75be23` on the server. Can you provide the SSH password or authorize my key?

> AGENT

Found the issue! The host directory `/sandcastle/data/users/thieso/home/` is owned by `sandcastle:sandcastle` with `755` permissions. Inside a Sysbox container with user namespace mapping, the container's root can't write to it.

Let me check the SandboxManager to see how the home directory is created and verify the UID mapping.

{

  "old_string": "  def ensure_mount_dirs(user, sandbox)\n    if sandbox.mount_home\n      FileUtils.mkdir_p(\"#{DATA_DIR}/users/#{user.name}/home\")\n    end\n    if sandbox.data_path.present?\n      dir = \"#{DATA_DIR}/users/#{user.name}/data/#{sandbox.data_path}\".chomp(\"/\")\n      FileUtils.mkdir_p(dir)\n    end\n  end",
  "new_string": "  def ensure_mount_dirs(user, sandbox)\n    # Directories bind-mounted into Sysbox containers must be world-writable\n    # because Sysbox maps container root to a high host UID (via /etc/subuid)\n    # that won't match the directory owner.\n    if sandbox.mount_home\n      FileUtils.mkdir_p(\"#{DATA_DIR}/users/#{user.name}/home\", mode: 0o777)\n    end\n    if sandbox.data_path.present?\n      dir = \"#{DATA_DIR}/users/#{user.name}/data/#{sandbox.data_path}\".chomp(\"/\")\n      FileUtils.mkdir_p(dir, mode: 0o777)\n    end\n    if sandbox.persistent_volume && sandbox.volume_path\n      FileUtils.mkdir_p(sandbox.volume_path, mode: 0o777)\n    end\n  end"
}

> AGENT

Now running `installer.sh update` will `chmod 777` all existing user home dirs, data dirs, and sandbox volumes so Sysbox containers can write to them. This runs after the `chown` so it won't be undone.

To summarize the three fixes:

1. **`installer.sh`** — `ensure_dirs` now `chmod 777` existing bind-mount dirs on update
2. **`sandbox_manager.rb`** — `ensure_mount_dirs` now `chmod 0o777` on every create/restore (handles new + existing dirs)
3. **`container_sync_job.rb`** — detects `State.Restarting` and marks sandbox as "stopped" instead of incorrectly showing "running"
4. **`application.html.erb`** — flash messages now render in the layout so errors aren't silently swallowed

There isn't one — the fix is the `chmod 777` loop, not a chown. But you're right to question this: the existing `chown -R` on line 147 is actually the **problem**. It recursively sets everything under `data/users` to UID 220568, which would also reset files *inside* user home dirs that Sysbox created with UID 231072.

The `chown -R` shouldn't recurse into bind-mounted directories. Let me fix that:

> AGENT

The `chown -R` on `data/users` and `data/sandboxes` recursively chowns everything to 220568 — including the contents of bind-mounted dirs that Sysbox containers wrote as UID 231072. That breaks file ownership inside containers. The fix: only chown the top-level dirs, not recurse into per-user bind-mount targets.

> TOOL

id: toolu_01E1cXoFoQuEkL43YcbysBjU

  "new_string": "  chown \"${SANDCASTLE_USER}:${SANDCASTLE_GROUP}\" \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"\n  # Own top-level data dirs (not -R: per-user subdirs are bind-mounted into\n  # Sysbox containers which use a different UID range via /etc/subuid).\n  chown \"${SANDCASTLE_UID}:${SANDCASTLE_GID}\" \\\n    \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/users \\\n    \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/sandboxes \\\n    \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/wetty\n  chown -R \"${SANDCASTLE_UID}:${SANDCASTLE_GID}\" \\\n    \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/traefik/dynamic\n  # Per-user dirs: own the user-level parent, then chmod 777 the bind-mount\n  # targets so Sysbox-mapped root can write to them.\n  for d in \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/users/*; do\n    [ -d \"$d\" ] && chown \"${SANDCASTLE_UID}:${SANDCASTLE_GID}\" \"$d\"\n  done\n  for d in \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/users/*/home \\\n           \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/users/*/data \\\n           \"$SANDCASTLE_HOME\"/data/sandboxes/*/vol; do\n    [ -d \"$d\" ] && chmod 777 \"$d\"\n  done"

> AGENT

There it is: **`Authentication refused: bad ownership or modes for directory /home/thieso`**

SSH's `StrictModes` rejects the login because `/home/thieso` is `777` — SSH requires the home directory to be writable **only** by the owner (max `755`). Our `chmod 777` fix breaks SSH auth.

The real fix: the home directory should be `755` but owned by the **Sysbox-mapped UID**, not world-writable. Let me rethink the approach.

> TOOL

2. Have `entrypoint.sh` tighten permissions to `755` after setup, so SSH's StrictModes is satisfied

> AGENT

Found it. `set -euo pipefail` is the problem. When `grep '^SANDCASTLE_USER='` finds no match (for non-sandbox containers like postgres, traefik), it returns exit code 1. With `pipefail`, that kills the whole script.
